Subject: Evaluation kickoff & success criteria — ClearBridge Analytics

Thanks again for the time earlier, Elena and Tom — really useful conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get your evaluation started next week.

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for your customer-facing scoring pipeline and reduce per-call latency while keeping model quality at parity.
- Key constraints: strict P95 latency targets, strict PII handling, and an internal prompts library (~600 prompts across use cases).
- Success signals you called out: parity on NDCG for top-5 reranking, P95 latency <250ms for request sizes typical of your pipeline, and an integration path for streaming outputs.

Proposed next step: schedule an evaluation kickoff (demo + technical deep dive). We suggest a 60–75 minute session to align on the trial plan, confirm success criteria, and collect a representative prompt set for the evals. Two windows that work on our side:
- Tue Feb 17, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Feb 18, 14:00–15:00 PT

Attachments: I’m attaching a short draft evaluation plan that outlines scope/duration and deliverables (clearbridge_eval_plan_v1.pdf). Please confirm which time works and who from your side should join (technical + security). Also let us know if you prefer Redwood Dedicated or a hosted evaluation for data handling reasons.

Thanks — happy to adjust. I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) and Karthik (AE) for the technical coordination.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / Tom — Rishi here (SE). Quick note on what I’ll cover during the technical portion and what will help us run a focused eval: 

Proposed technical agenda (45–50 mins)
- Quick demo of Redwood serving runtime + routing/fallback behavior (10 mins)
- Integration patterns and API walkthrough (10 mins)
- Live example: run 5–10 of your sample prompts to validate latency/quality (15–20 mins)
- Eval mechanics: metric capture, prompt set validation, and dashboarding (10 mins)

What we’ll need from you ahead of the call
- Representative prompt set in CSV (sample_prompt_set.csv works) — include expected outputs/labels where available.
- A short note on which model family you want us to prioritize (instructions/LLM type) and top success metric (NDCG, Precision@k, etc.).
- Any IP/PII constraints or files we shouldn’t persist.

Regarding the SOC2/data handling doc — Olga, do we have a short package we can share prior to the meeting? If needed we can redact anything sensitive for the initial review.

Thanks — I’ll be ready to run a live loop with a sandbox key.

Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Great — thanks for confirming, Elena. Officially booked for Tue Feb 17, 10:00–11:00 PT. Calendar invite attached (calendar_invite.ics) and a Google Meet link is included in the event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=cb_eval_20260217_1000PT

Attachments I’ve included for the meeting:
- clearbridge_eval_plan_v1.pdf (draft scope, 4-week plan, deliverables, roles)
- sample_prompt_set.csv (placeholders — please replace with your 50-row sample)

Quick clarifications based on the thread:
- Evaluation length: 4 weeks (can be shortened/extended based on results).
- Success criteria (draft): P95 latency <250ms on typical request sizes; parity or improvement on existing reranking NDCG_top5; predictable token cost under our proposed config.
- Environment: we’ll run the initial eval on Redwood Hosted with an option to move to Dedicated if you need network isolation.

Elena — I’ll also send our SOC 2 summary and data handling one-pager to Maya separately (expect that in an hour). If there are any last-minute attendees to add, reply-all and I’ll update the invite.

Looking forward to it.

Best,
